title: slot-shepherd-and-spillback-rate-limiter: fragmentation mitigator for KV cache residency
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: reduce long-term fragmentation and repeated spill cycles in the KV cache under mixed-size tenant workloads without increasing p99 latency. Fragmentation and frequent small spillovers were causing extra I/O, elevated token latency on tail workloads, and uneven tenant cost. This PR implements a "slot shepherd" residency strategy plus a coordinated spillback rate limiter and scheduler hints to improve compaction opportunities and reduce reactive paging. Key ideas: 1) Fragmentation score: compact, workload-aware metric that favors slots with low coalescing potential for eviction while preserving multi-slot contiguous regions when possible. 2) Slot shepherd: delay-and-coalesce eviction path that defers non-critical evictions for a short bounded window to allow adjacent free slots to manifest, enabling in-place compaction and avoiding unnecessary spill I/O. 3) Spillback rate limiter: global and tenant-scoped leaky-bucket limiter that prevents cascaded spillovers when a tenant's working set temporarily exceeds reservation; it exposes backpressure signals to the scheduler to slow ingestion and trigger KV cache-aware batching. 4) Scheduler integration: the runtime scheduler receives compactness hints and preferred kernel selection markers to favor kernels optimized for partially filled pages (reducing memcpy overhead). 5) Continuous batching interaction: small changes in batching policy so that the delay window cooperates with continuous batching to avoid increasing p50/p90 latency while improving throughput. Implementation notes: added fragmentation scoring code in engine/kv/fragment_score.cc, slot shepherd state machine in engine/kv/slot_shepherd.{cc,h}, a spillback limiter in engine/kv/spill_limiter.{cc,h}, and lightweight hooks from scheduler/api to propagate hints. Added unit and integration tests in tests/kv/ to cover degenerate small-object workloads and tenant-fairness scenarios. Observability: new metrics kv.fragmentation_score, kv.shepherd_deferrals, kv.spillback_tokens_used, and alerting runbook updates in observability/alerts/kv_fragmentation.md. Rollout plan: feature-flag guarded, canary enabled on dedicated pools with 10% traffic for 72h, smoke verification checklist enforced via linear task ENG-1982. Backwards compatibility: no change to external API; eviction behavior is behind a flag and defaults to off for older clusters. Related work: builds on earlier paging allocator improvements (ENG-1457) and ties to continuous batching improvements (ENG-1701).

review_conversation: Daniel Hsu: The fragmentation score looks reasonable but can you clarify worst-case CPU overhead? Aisha: Score is O(1) per slot update, we sample on allocation/eviction boundaries and added a budgeted background scanner to avoid hot paths. Priya Raman: Request change: add tenant fairness test for heavy small-object churn. Aisha: Added tests in tests/kv/test_spillback_rate_limiter.cc and adjusted limiter behavior to be tenant-scoped. Omar Castillo: Minor nit on naming (shepherd vs steward) but overall LGTM. CI: initial run failed a flaky kernel selection test, reran and it passed, full CI green. Merge: squash merge after canary metrics met criteria, post-merge follow-up to tune default deferral window.
release_notes: Introduces slot shepherd eviction strategy and a spillback rate limiter to reduce KV cache fragmentation and reactive spillovers. Feature gated and enabled via canary. New metrics: kv.fragmentation_score, kv.shepherd_deferrals, kv.spillback_tokens_used. Expected impact: reduced spill I/O and improved tail latency for mixed-size workloads when enabled.
notes: Canary observed ~28% reduction in small-spill events and 6% improvement in p99 token latency on a 10k qps mixed workload. Follow-ups: tune deferral window per instance type (ENG-2105) and add an opt-in compact-on-evict mode for on-prem customers.
